$description: Struct-level golden vectors for canonicalBoxBytes — the box identity encoding that computeBoxId and computeTxId hash (TYPES_INTERFACE -> Layout - Boxes). A positional layout, with `guard` absent from the consensus bytes. One vector per box type, because the per-type field lists are seven separate layouts sharing a two-field prefix — plus a second bond vector, because `bond.inviteePublicKey` is the one 0-or-32-byte field in the box arms and its two states are two encodings, not one, and a second genesis_proof vector, because an empty payload is what its length prefix exists for.

vectors.name: box/karma-minimal
vectors.note: 43 bytes, down from 114. The CBOR form spent a two-byte map header, five key names and nine bytes on a value of 100; this spends one tag byte, one value byte and no key names at all. Trailing 00 is the absent decayBurn option.

vectors.name: box/karma-decay-burn
vectors.note: The option present, and a real production proofSource. `decay-70000` is what node's decay service actually stamps — which is the evidence that karma.proofSource is lpUtf8 and not b32: a fixed-width writer would throw on every karma mint the node performs.

vectors.name: box/karma-value-u64-max
vectors.note: The whole argument for the bigint exception, in one vector: those ten bytes are the all-ones sentinel a malformed NUMBER field takes, and here they are a perfectly legal box value. `value: bigint` spans the entire u64, so no sentinel is unreachable and its writer has to throw instead — sentinelling would give a malformed box a well-formed box's id.

vectors.name: box/credit-transfer-sentinel
vectors.note: Why credit.proofSource is vlqS. Production stamps -1 here as the transfer marker on every user-path credit box, so an unsigned writer would sentinel every transfer the node makes. ZigZag maps -1 to 1: one byte.

vectors.name: box/credit-wide
vectors.note: value > 2^53 — the range a `number` cannot hold, which is why box values are bigint at all. proofSource 70000 is above 65536 and carries the wide-int pin (it moved here from the deleted createdAtBlock). lockedUntilBlock present, so the option's other branch is covered on this type too.

vectors.name: box/invite
vectors.note: Two adjacent b32 fields with distinct values, so a swap of secretHash and inviterId shows up here rather than as a moved id much later.

vectors.name: box/genesis-proof-typical
vectors.note: The only arm whose whole tail is one lp field, and the only type whose value is fixed at 0 — the box holds neither karma nor credits, so it never enters supply accounting. `0d` is the payload's length prefix: the field is lp and not lpUtf8 because the bytes are opaque to consensus, so a conformance reader must not attempt UTF-8 on them. Production content is the per-network NetworkProfile.genesisProofPayload; this vector's is its own.

vectors.name: box/genesis-proof-empty-payload
vectors.note: Three bytes — the smallest legal box of any type, and the case that pins why the payload is length-prefixed. Appended raw, an empty payload would be indistinguishable from the end of the box, and a one-byte payload of 00 would encode as 030000 too. Here the trailing 00 is the count, and a one-byte payload of 00 is 03000100.

vectors.name: box/bond-committed
vectors.note: The widest layout: five fields after the prefix, alternating fixed-width and VLQ. The `01` before the invitee key is the option's PRESENT tag: this field is 0-or-32 bytes, so it is `opt(b32)` and not `b32`. 71 bytes, one more than the b32 form this replaced (2026-08-09).

vectors.name: box/bond-unclaimed
vectors.note: The SAME bond before commit, and the shape production actually creates: node rejects an invite-create whose bond output carries a key, because a pre-committed bond would let the inviter reclaim immediately and make the network's only sybil cost free. Under the b32 row this vector had no encoding at all — `writeBytesNOrThrow` threw on the empty field, so `computeTxId` threw on every invite creation. Both halves of the injectivity claim sit in these two vectors: `00` versus `01 ‖ 32 bytes`, differing in the first byte after `inviteOutputIndex`, so an unclaimed bond can never share an encoding with a committed one. Decode direction earns its keep here — absent must come back as EMPTY bytes, not null, or the re-encode compare fails.

vectors.name: box/post-lock
vectors.note: value 3 and originalValue 5 are deliberately different — a lock that has vested. Two bigints back to back, so a swap is visible. targetPostId is the only hex-string field on any box type and crosses as 32 raw bytes like every other id.

vectors.name: box/vouch
vectors.note: Value is always 1 karma on this type, so the vector's job is the two identity fields and the tag.

rejects.name: box/genesis-proof-payload-over-bound
rejects.note: A 513-byte payload, one past MAX_GENESIS_PROOF_PAYLOAD_BYTES. Every byte of it is present and the lp field is well formed, so nothing here is truncated and nothing re-encodes differently - the bound is the only rule that can refuse these bytes, and 8104 is the count that makes them 513 rather than 512. The bound is per-type and lives in the genesis_proof arm of the reader, never in readLp, which every lp field shares; box/genesis-proof-typical is the same layout inside the bound. An over-bound payload still ENCODES, exactly as an unknown boxType does - the writers are total and the refusal is one-way.

rejects.name: box/unassigned-tag-7
rejects.note: 7 is the first tag the table does not assign, and an unassigned tag has no decoding at all — the reader refuses it rather than skipping to the next field. Distinct from box/unknown-tag-255 below: 0xff is the sentinel an unknown boxType WRITES, while this is simply a number nothing claims, and both must be one-way.

rejects.name: box/unknown-tag-255
rejects.note: 0xff is what enum8 WRITES for an unknown boxType, and it must not decode back into anything. That one-wayness is why the tag writer can stay total where the fixed-width writers cannot: a malformed box encodes, but never as a valid one.

rejects.name: box/non-minimal-value
rejects.note: box/karma-minimal with `value` padded from 64 to e4 00. It decodes to 100 either way — only the re-encode compare rejects it, and this is the field a malleability attempt would target because it is what a box is worth.

rejects.name: box/trailing-byte
rejects.note: box/karma-minimal plus a byte. Appended junk is a rejection, not slack — the defect class this format exists to close is junk riding inside a committed structure.

rejects.name: box/bond-option-tag-2
rejects.note: box/bond-unclaimed with the option tag flipped from 00 to 02. `opt` has exactly two tags and a third is a rejection, not a third state — which is the property `opt(b32)` was chosen for over `lp`: an `lp` here would have accepted the byte as a length and round-tripped a 2-byte invitee key, leaving the 0-or-32 domain entirely to validation.

rejects.name: box/bond-committed-short-key
rejects.note: The option's PRESENT branch with 31 bytes of key instead of 32. The other half of the structural claim: `00` means absent and `01` means exactly 32 bytes, so there is no third encoding and a short key has none at all rather than sharing one with a valid bond.

rejects.name: box/invalid-utf8-proofSource
rejects.note: A one-byte proofSource of 0xff, which is not valid UTF-8 in any position. Rejected by readLpUtf8's fatal decoder rather than replaced with U+FFFD — a lossy decode would map two distinct byte strings onto one value and the re-encode compare could only report it as `non-canonical`, naming the wrong fault.
